summary: kmf-vendor-pack ships install-time beacon to hardcoded IP via opaque native addon
details: kmf-vendor-pack@100.100.101 is a hollow npm package whose `index.js` exports an empty object and whose only functional artifact is a prebuilt Linux ELF at `prebuilds/linux-x64/addon.node`. The `postinstall` hook (`postinstall.js`) requires that addon, and its NAPI module-init collects installer identity (gethostname, getuid/getpwuid) together with the npm environment (`npm_package_name`, `npm_config_registry`) and opens a raw TCP socket to the hardcoded IPv4 address 64.181.165.115, issuing `POST /dc HTTP/1.0` with a `h=&u=&p=&r=` body carrying those values over plain HTTP. The tarball ships no C/C++ sources, no `binding.gyp`, and no build toolchain, so the native code is opaque and runs automatically on `npm install`. The package's stated purpose ("Frontend utilities") does not match its contents: it has no library surface, and the addon's sole observable behavior is the install-time beacon to the hardcoded IP.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
